outcome.technical: Closed the receive-pack gap. tools/sweep-selftests.py: run_one now allocates a per-child directory (mkdtemp prefix sg-) outside both watched channels, writes a runner-owned git config holding receive.autogc=false into it (git_global_env) and points the child's GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL at it; git_global_debris() reads it back with scratch_debris so a suite's `git config --global` (which now lands there instead of the watched home) is reported, labelled 'git global config'. The file carries receive.autogc ONLY: a probe (git 2.53) showed that key alone takes the receive-pack spawn to zero, and copying maintenance.auto/gc.auto into it turned test_commit_task_work.py's ctw-nm2 deny twin red (that suite strips only the GIT_CONFIG_COUNT pairs to measure its prefix alone), so the file is held to the one key receive-pack reads. Probes: GIT_CONFIG_COUNT set -> 1 spawn on push; global file with receive.autogc=false -> 0; empty global -> 1; `-c maintenance.auto=false -c gc.auto=0` on the push -> 1 (lost too).
